pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] allow non-power-of-two head sizes in prefix prefill
pr_body:
The existing prefix prefill kernel only supports head dimension that is a power of two. This due to Triton only supporting power of two block sizes. This PR enlarges the Q,K,V tensors to the next power of two and pads them with zeros when reading (and writing). It doesn't seem to affect performance of the non-padded case. CC @rkooo567 FIX #4127 ---

issue_context.title: [Bug][Chunked prefill]: head size has to be power of two
issue_context.body:

The chunked prefill doesn't support head sizes that are not powers of two. For example, phi2 has head size of 80 (which is supported by flash attn, but the _flash_fwd triton kernel doesn't support it).

Fix PR is coming.

sampling_params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.8)
llm = LLM(model="microsoft/phi-2", enable_chunked_prefill=True)
print(llm.generate("Hello, ", sampling_params))

review_comments: This condition seems to be shared across all conditions, is this correct? If so, should we create a separate mask that combines 2?

The conditions are actually subtly different for each `tl.load()`. My limited understanding of Triton is that it will inline the condition in the load operation, so I think it's better to keep two separate 1D tensors rather the pre-computing the 2D matrix anyways.
